answer: Unrepeatable challenge lineage. Each agent identity is seeded by a sable hash chain whose next link encodes a fresh, verifiable challenge drawn from live network state; registration requires solving that instance and publishing the derivation path, so replaying a prior solution fails. Identities also commit a small glacier-paced cooldown, forcing attackers to serialize work across epochs. The timber cost is per-identity compute plus latency, and mass registration scales linearly in real wall-clock time, making farms economically uncompetitive.
